title: Stage 3: Selectors
summary: Derive what the UI shows: filtered, sorted task lists, counts and tag lists.

steps.title: Derive, do not store
body: The board stores only tasks. Everything the screen shows (the filtered list, column counts, the tag cloud) is **derived** by **selectors**: pure functions of the state.
const counts = countByStatus(board);        // { todo: 2, doing: 1, done: 1 }

Storing derived data (a `todoCount` field, a `filteredTasks` array) means keeping it in sync on every change, and it will drift. In React, selectors run during render; wrap them in `useMemo` only if they are measurably slow.
Selectors must not reorder or mutate the board: use `toSorted`, not `sort`.

steps.prompt: A teammate adds `visibleTasks: Task[]` to `Board` and updates it in every reducer case. What is the main risk?
options: It can get out of sync with `tasks`, a bug class that disappears if it is computed by a selector
TypeScript cannot type arrays inside objects

code: const rank = { high: 0, medium: 1, low: 2 } as const;
const sorted = tasks.toSorted((x, y) => rank[x.priority] - rank[y.priority] || x.createdAt - y.createdAt);
steps.explain: Priority first; among equal priorities, older first. `toSorted` leaves `tasks` alone.

steps.title: selectTasks, countByStatus, allTags
prompt: Add three selectors to your code:
type Filter = { status?: Status; priority?: Priority; tag?: string; search?: string };

- `selectTasks(board: Board, filter: Filter = {}): Task[]`: keep tasks matching **every** given filter (`tag` and `search` are trimmed and case-insensitive; `search` looks in the title), sorted by priority (high, medium, low), then by `createdAt` ascending. Do not change the board.
- `countByStatus(board): Record<Status, number>`: always has all three keys.

type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };

return { ok: true, value: { id, title, status: "todo", priority, tags, createdAt: now } };
function updateTask(board: Board, id: string, change: (t: Task) => Task): Board {
function boardReducer(board: Board, action: Action): Board {
return updateTask(board, action.id, t => (t.title === title ? t : { ...t, title }));
return updateTask(board, action.id, t => (t.status === action.status ? t : { ...t, status: action.status }));
return updateTask(board, action.id, t => (t.priority === action.priority ? t : { ...t, priority: action.priority }));
